headline: High-risk default interaction: Open Interpreter can read/write the filesystem and execute code, while LightZero is non-runnable and isolated, so the main hazards are leakage, conflict, and cascading misuse from the automation side.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no documented I/O bridge or filesystem access, so it cannot directly inject Open Interpreter by default. Open Interpreter can read clipboard/files and execute code, so if an operator manually copies LightZero-generated text into it, prompt injection becomes possible, but the bridge is manual and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF the operator copies LightZero output into Open Interpreter input
IF Open Interpreter is run with clipboard or file ingestion enabled
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting model output into Open Interpreter
Disable clipboard-based ingestion during paired runs
Use a plain-text sanitizer before transfer
Keep LightZero outputs in a separate read-only note
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress, while LightZero is open-source docs-only and touches no data classes. The pair can leak local files if Open Interpreter is pointed at sensitive directories, even though LightZero itself does not expose data; the shared local machine surface makes this plausible in default desktop use.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is run on a machine containing sensitive local files
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to transmit file contents to configured model providers
mitigations: Run Open Interpreter in a dedicated user account
Restrict its working directory to a non-sensitive folder
Disable network egress for the session
Move secrets off the local machine before use
requires-engineering: sandbox Open Interpreter in Docker

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capabilities, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. LightZero has no write or shell capability, so it will not contend directly, but the pair still creates dangerous default conflicts if both touch the same workspace through Open Interpreter-driven automation; uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter and another process share the same writable workspace
IF Open Interpreter modifies git state while other instances are active
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per run
Pause other writers before starting Open Interpreter
Commit or stash changes first
Limit Open Interpreter to a throwaway repo clone
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing agent with no action-taking authority, while Open Interpreter can execute shell commands and modify files. If LightZero output is treated as authoritative by Open Interpreter, the latter can turn a mistaken recommendation into real actions; the pathway exists, but LightZero is not inherently an action planner, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes LightZero output as instructions without verification
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to execute the resulting commands
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Ask Open Interpreter to restate assumptions before acting
Keep LightZero outputs advisory only
Log every command for rollback
requires-engineering: add schema validation for transferred outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for LightZero, and Open Interpreter’s docs only show local-machine access plus user-configured model providers. The main compliance issue is operational: if regulated data is present on the local machine, Open Interpreter can access it, but the pair does not itself establish a residency breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored on the local machine during Open Interpreter use
IF the configured model provider is outside the required residency boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the workstation
Use a residency-approved model provider
Review retention settings before each session
Separate personal and regulated workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss controls at the OS boundary
